TYPE 1 ZONING MAP AMENDMENT!
NARRATIVE

The subject property is located at 3444-3446 W. North Ave., Chicago, IL 60647. The Jot is 6,800
square feet. The property measures 50 feet along the W. North Ave. frontage and 136 feet along
the N. St. Louis Ave. frontage. Currently, the property is vacant/unimproved.

The property is owned by ASI (the “Applicant’”).

The Applicant seeks to rezone the subject property from B3-1, Community Shopping District to
B3-3, Community Shopping District to develop a 20,400 SF, 58’-4” high, five-story building for
office use by the Applicant. The site will have two (2) off-street parking spaces one (1) of which
will be ADA accessible. There will be six (6) bicycle parking spaces and one (1) loading space.
Pursuant to Section 17-20207, office use is permitted by-right in the B3-3 district.

(a) Floor Area Ratio. Pursuant to Section 17-2-0403-A, the maximum FAR in the B3-3
district is 3.0. The proposed project’s FAR is 3.0 (i.e., 20,400 SF building area + 6,800 SF lot
area = 3.0). Therefore, the project will conform to the FAR standards.

(b) Minimum Lot Area. The minimum lot area regulations under Section 17-3-0402 do not
apply because the proposed project is not residential.

(c) Off-street Parking. Pursuant to Section 17-10-0207-L, the minimum vehicle parking
requirement for the project (i.e., office use) is none for the first 10,000 SF then 2 spaces per

1,000 SF. The minimum bike parking requirement is 1 per 10 auto spaces. Based on these
regulations, the minimum parking requirement is 21 spaces and the minimum bike parking
requirement is 2 spaces. Pursuant to Section 17-10-0902-A, based on the minimum parking
requirement, the minimum number of accessible spaces required is 1 (one) space. The project
will have two (2) vehicle parking spaces, one (1) of which will be ADA accessible, and six (6)
bike parking spaces. Therefore, the project does not conform with the minimum parking
requirement. However, pursuant to Section 17-10-0102-B-1-(a), in all districts except D districts,
minimum off-street automobile parking ratios may be reduced by up to 100 percent from the
otherwise applicable standards for new construction or rehabilitation or reuse of existing
structures located within 2,640 feet of a CTA rail station entrance or exit or within 1,320 feet of a
CTA bus line corridor roadway segment listed in Table 17-17-0400-B. The minimum parking
requirement for the project may be reduced by up to 100 percent because the project is: (1) new
construction; and (2) located within 1,320 feet of a CTA bus line corridor roadway segment listed
in Table 17-17-0400-B (i.e., the project is located on North Ave. within the CTA bus line corridor
roadway segment from Harlem Ave. to Clark St.). Pursuant to Section 17-10-0102-B-(c), the
Applicant seeks an administrative adjustment to reduce the minimum required parking from 21

RE: ASI Multi Functional Training Center — Landscape Narrative

The project is a 5-story trade school at the corner of W North Ave and St Louis St in
Chicago. The amenities in the project are a small entrance plaza, parkway trees and lawn,
and a small parking lot on the first floor, and outdoor terraces on the 3° and 5" floors.

This landscape narrative is based on the floor plans provided by UrbanWorks on
9/22/2025. This narrative is a DRAFT for preliminary pricing. Materials are suggested
and quantities are approximate only. The contractor should verify specifications,
dimensions, and quantities in the architectural and engineering drawings.

1ST FLOOR,
Demolition:
1, Existing concrete: 1746 sq. ft. of concrete in St Louis St parkway to be demolished.

2, Existing soil: 3492 cubic feet of soil will be removed from the St Louis St parkway.
3. Tree grates: 3 existing metal tree grates in St Louis St to be removed.

Hardscape:

1. Pavers: 365 SF of pavers at the building entrance. Pavers. Treo Smooth permeable
pavers by Unilock or similar will be installed over a 4” layer of aggregate to allow
percolation. (Verify in civil engineering drawings if a thicker layer of aggregate is
needed for water detention purposes),

2, Edging: 143 Lineal feet of polymeric sand will be around the pavers. If a flexible joint
is required, a 70 lineal feet border between the pavers and the building, and 73 lineal
feet between the pavers and the concrete in the sidewalk could be provided.

3. Fences: The Chicago Landscape Ordinance requires parking lot screening for any
vehicular use area 1200 sq. ft. or larger. The current proposed parking lot is 740 sq.
ft., therefore, it should not require parking lot screening. The Chicago Landscape
Ordinances do not require internal planting for parking lots 3000 sq, ft. or less.

4. Benches: 2- Float backed, 6-foot, aluminum frame, FSC 100% Ipé hardwood slats by
Forms + Surfaces or similar.
